mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 0.3 percentage points signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline in periods where UNRATE rises > 0.3pp (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 6-month decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) exceeding 2% signals deteriorating household demand, which reduces earnings growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline in periods where GDPC1 falls > 2% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous 3-month decline in FEDFUNDS and a rise in CPIAUCSL above 3% signals a failed easing cycle with persistent inflation, which erodes real earnings and produces negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS falls and CPIAUCSL rises > 3% over 3 months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline in periods where FEDFUNDS falls and CPIAUCSL rises > 3% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in payroll employment above 0.5% signals labor market tightening, which raises wage pressure and compresses profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline in periods where PAYEMS rises > 0.5% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month decline in industrial production (INDPRO) exceeding 1% signals weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces earnings growth and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline in periods where INDPRO falls > 1% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the Housing Starts Index (HOUST) above 5% signals stronger residential investment, which boosts construction-related earnings and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline in periods where HOUST rises > 5% (t-test p > 0.05).
